Here $(P_n,\theta_n)\in \{(P,\theta):P \in \mathcal{P},\theta \in \Theta_I(P)\}$ is a subsequence as defined in \eqref{eq:cover3}-\eqref{eq:pi_def} below,  $\theta_n^\prime \in (\theta_n +\rho /\sqrt{n} B^d)\cap \Theta$, $B^d = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^d:|x_i| \le 1, i=1,\dots,d\}$, $B^d_{n,\rho}\equiv \frac{\sqrt n}{\rho }(\Theta-\theta_n)\cap B^d$, $\mathfrak B^d_\rho=\lim_{n\to\infty}B^d_{n,\rho}$, and $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^d$.}\label{table:notation}} \smallskip



\resizebox{20cm}{!}{

\begin{tabular}{lllllllllllllllll}
\hline \hline
\\ 
$\mathbb{G}_{n,j}(\cdot) $ & $=$ & $ \frac{\sqrt n (\bar{m}_{n,j}(\cdot) - E_P(m_j(X_i,\cdot)))}{\sigma_{P,j}(\cdot)},~j=1,\dots,J$ & Sample empirical process.\\ 
[0.2cm]
$\mathbb{G}_{n,j}^b(\cdot) $ & $=$ & $ \frac{\sqrt n (\bar{m}^b_{n,j}(\cdot) - \bar{m}_{n,j}(\cdot))}{\hat{\sigma}_{n,j}(\cdot)},~j=1,\dots,J$ & Bootstrap empirical process. \\ 
[0.2cm]
$\eta_{n,j}(\cdot) $ & $=$ & $ \frac{\sigma_{P,j}(\cdot)}{\hat{\sigma}_{n,j}(\cdot)}-1,~j=1,\dots,J$ & Estimation error in sample moments' asymptotic standard deviation.\\
[0.2cm]
$D_{P,j}(\cdot) $ & $=$ & $ \nabla_\theta \left(\frac{E_P(m_j(X_i,\cdot))}{\sigma_{P,j}(\cdot)} \right),~j=1,\dots,J$ & Gradient of population moments w.r.t. $\theta$, with estimator $\hat{D}_{n,j}(\cdot) $. \\
[0.2cm]
$\gamma_{1,P_n,j}(\cdot) $ & $=$ & $ \frac{E_{P_n}(m_j(X_i,\cdot))}{\sigma_{P_n,j}(\cdot)},~j=1,\dots,J$ & Studentized population moments. \\
[0.4cm]
$\pi_{1,j}$ & $=$ & $\lim_{n \to \infty} \kappa_{n}^{-1} \sqrt {n} \gamma_{1,P_n,j}(\theta_{n}^\prime)$ & Limit of rescaled population moments, constant $\forall \theta_n^\prime \in (\theta_n +\rho /\sqrt{n} B^d)\cap \Theta$\\
 &  &  & by Lemma \ref{lem:Jstar}.\\
$\pi_{1,j}^*$ & $=$ & $\left\{ \begin{matrix}
   0, & \mathrm{if}~\pi_{1,j}=0,\\
   -\infty, & \mathrm{if}~\pi_{1,j}<0.
\end{matrix}\right.$ & ``Oracle" GMS.\\
[0.4cm]
$\hat{\xi}_{n,j}(\cdot)$ & $=$ & $\left\{\begin{array}{ll}
\kappa_n^{-1}\sqrt n\bar m_{n,j}(\cdot)/\hat\sigma_{n,j}(\cdot), & j=1,\dots,J_1 \\ 
0, & j=J_1+1,\dots,J
\end{array}\right.$  & Rescaled studentized sample moments, set to $0$ for equalities. \\
[0.5cm]
$\varphi^*_j(\xi)$& $=$ & $\begin{cases}
	\varphi_j(\xi)&\pi_{1,j}=0\\
	-\infty&\pi_{1,j}<0\\
	0&j=J_1+1,\cdots,J.
\end{cases}$ & Infeasible GMS that is less conservative than $\varphi_j$.  \\
[0.5cm]
$u_{n,j,\theta_n}(\lambda)$ & $=$ &  $\{\mathbb G_{n,j}(\theta_n+\frac{\lambda \rho }{\sqrt n})+\rho D_{P_n,j}(\bar{\theta}_n)\lambda+\pi^*_{1,j}\}(1+\eta_{n,j}(\theta_n+\frac{\lambda \rho }{\sqrt n}))$ & Mean value expansion of nonlinear constraints with sample empirical process \\
 &  &  & and ``oracle" GMS, with $\bar{\theta}_n$ componentwise between $\theta_n$ and $\theta_n+\frac{\lambda \rho }{\sqrt n}$.\\
[0.4cm]
$U_n(\theta_n,c)$ & $=$ &  $\big\{\lambda\in B^d_{n,\rho}: p^\prime \lambda = 0 \cap u_{n,j,\theta_n}(\lambda)\le c, \: \forall j=1,\dots,J\big\}$ & Feasible set for nonlinear sample problem intersected with $p^\prime \lambda=0$.\\
[0.4cm]
$\mathfrak{w}_{j}(\lambda)$ & $=$ & $\mathbb{Z}_{j}+\rho D_{j}\lambda+\pi^*_{1,j}$ & Linearized constraints with a Gaussian shift and ``oracle'' GMS.   \\
[0.4cm]
$\mathfrak W(c)$ & $=$ & $\big\{\lambda\in \mathfrak B^d_\rho: p^\prime \lambda = 0 \cap \mathfrak w_{j}(\lambda)\le c, \: \forall j=1,\dots,J\big\}$ & Feasible set for linearized limit problem intersected with $p'\lambda=0$.
\\
[0.4cm]
$c_{\pi^*}$ &$=$ & $\inf\{c\in\mathbb R_+:\mathrm{Pr}(\mathfrak{W}(c)\ne\emptyset)\ge 1-\alpha\}$.& Limit problem critical level.
\\
[0.4cm]
$v^b_{n,j,\theta_n^\prime}(\lambda)$ & $=$ &  $\mathbb G^b_{n,j}(\theta_n^\prime)+\rho \hat{D}_{n,j}(\theta_n^\prime)\lambda+\varphi_j(\hat{\xi}_{n,j}(\theta_n^\prime))$ & Linearized constraints with bootstrap empirical process and sample GMS.\\
[0.4cm]
$V_n^b(\theta_n^\prime,c)$ & $=$ &  $\big\{ \lambda\in B^d_{n,\rho}: p^\prime \lambda = 0 \cap v^b_{n,j,\theta_n^\prime}(\lambda)\le c, \: \forall j=1,\dots,J\big\}$ & Feasible set for linearized bootstrap problem with sample GMS and $p^\prime \lambda=0$. &\\
[0.4cm]
$v^I_{n,j,\theta_n^\prime}(\lambda)$ & $=$ &  $\mathbb G^b_{n,j}(\theta_n^\prime)+\rho \hat{D}_{n,j}(\theta_n^\prime)\lambda+\varphi^*_j(\hat{\xi}_{n,j}(\theta_n^\prime))$ & Linearized constraints with bootstrap empirical process and infeasible sample GMS.\\
[0.4cm]
$V_n^I(\theta_n^\prime,c)$ & $=$ &  $\big\{ \lambda\in B^d_{n,\rho}: p^\prime \lambda = 0 \cap v^I_{n,j,\theta_n^\prime}(\lambda)\le c, \: \forall j=1,\dots,J\big\}$ & Feasible set for linearized bootstrap problem with infeasible sample GMS and $p^\prime \lambda=0$. &\\
[0.4cm]










$\hat c_n(\theta)$ & $=$ &  $\inf\{c\in\mathbb R_+:P^*(V_n^b(\theta,c)\neq \emptyset)\ge 1-\alpha\}$ & Bootstrap critical level.\\
[0.2cm]
$\hat c_{n,\rho}(\theta)$ & $=$ & $\inf_{\lambda \in B^d_{n,\rho}} \hat{c}_n(\theta+\frac{\lambda\rho }{\sqrt n})$ & Smallest value of the bootstrap critical level in a $B^d_{n,\rho}$ neighborhood of $\theta$.\\
[0.2cm]
$\hat \sigma_{n,j}^M(\theta)$ & $=$ & $\hat \mu_{n,j}(\theta)\hat\sigma_{n,j}(\theta)+(1-\hat \mu_{n,j}(\theta))\hat\sigma_{n,j+R_1}(\theta)$ & Weighted sum of the estimators of the standard deviations of paired inequalities \\
[0.2cm]
\hline \hline
\end{tabular}
}

kappa_n^-1sqrtnsigma_P_n,j^-1(theta_n^prime)E_P_n[m_j(X_i,theta_n^prime)] Vert =o_P(1). \\ [0.15cm] Lemma & forall eta>0 ~exists delta>0, : Pr(\mathfrak W(c)neemptyset\cap \mathfrak W^-delta(c)=emptyset\)<eta, and similarly for V^I_n. \\ & It is unlikely that these sets are nonempty but become empty upon slightly tightening stochastic constraints.\\ [0.15cm] Lemma & Intersections of constraints whose gradients are almost linearly dependent are unlikely to realize inside W. \\ & Hence, we can ignore irregularities that occur as linear dependence is approached.\\ [0.15cm] Lemma & If there are weakly more equality constraints than parameters, then c is uniformly bounded away from zero.\\ & This simplifies some arguments.\\ [0.15cm] Lemma & If two paired inequalities are local to binding, then they are also asymptotically identical up to sign.\\ & This justifies ``merging" them.\\ [0.15cm] Lemma & eta_n,j(cdot) converges to zero uniformly in P and theta.\\ [0.15cm] hline hline

\parbox{20cm}{\caption[Table Flow]{Heuristics for the role of each Lemma in the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:validity}. Notes: (i) Uniformity in Theorem \ref{thm:validity} is enforced arguing along subsequences; (ii) When needed, random variables are realized on the same probability space as shown in Lemma \ref{lem:val} and Lemma \ref{cor:asrep} (see Appendix \ref{app:asrep} for details); (iii) Here $(P_n,\theta_n)\in \{(P,\theta):P \in \mathcal{P},\theta \in \Theta_I(P)\}$ is a subsequence as defined in \eqref{eq:cover3}-\eqref{eq:pi_def} below; (iv) All results hold for any $\theta_n^\prime \in (\theta_n +\rho /\sqrt{n} B^d)\cap \Theta$.}\label{table:flow}} \smallskip




\resizebox{20cm}{!}{
\begin{tabular}{lllllllllllllllll}
\hline \hline
 \\
Theorem \ref{thm:validity} & $P_n(p'\theta_n \in CI) \geq P_n\left(U_{n}(\theta_{n},\hat{c}_{n,\rho}(\theta_{n}))\neq \emptyset\right).$\\ 
 & Coverage is conservatively estimated by the probability that $U_{n}$ is nonempty. \\ 
[0.15cm]
Lemma \ref{lem:val} & $\liminf P_n\left(U_{n}(\theta_{n},\hat{c}_{n,\rho}(\theta_{n}))\neq \emptyset\right)\geq 1-\alpha.$\\
[0.15cm]
Lemma \ref{lem:UnonEmpty} & $P_n(U(\theta_n,c^I_n(\theta_{n}))\neq \emptyset ,\mathfrak W(c_{\pi^*})=\emptyset )+P_n(U(\theta_n,c^I_n(\theta_{n}))=\emptyset ,\mathfrak W(c_{\pi^*})\neq \emptyset)=o_{\mathcal{P}}(1).$ \\
 & Argued by comparing $U_n$ and its limit $\mathfrak W$ (after coupling).\\
[0.15cm]
Lemma \ref{lem:cv_convergence} & $P^*_n(V^I_n(\theta'_n,c)\ne\emptyset)-	\Pr(\mathfrak{W}(c)\ne\emptyset)\to 0$ and  $c^I_n(\theta'_n)\stackrel{P_n}{\to}c_{\pi^*}$ if $c_{\pi^*}>0$.\\
 & The bootstrap critical value that uses the less conservative GMS yileds a convergent critical value.\\
[0.15cm]
Lemma \ref{lem:res} & $\sup_{\lambda\in B^d} | \max_{j}(u_{n,j,\theta_{n}}(\lambda)-c^I_{n}(\theta_n))-\max_{j}(\mathfrak w_{j}(\lambda)-c_{\pi^*})|=o_\mathcal{P}(1)$, and similarly for $\mathfrak w_{j}$ and $v^I_{n,j,\theta_{n}^\prime}$.\\
 &  The criterion functions entering $U_n$ and $\mathfrak W$ converge to each other.
\\
[0.15cm]
Lemma \ref{lem:Jstar} & Local-to-binding constraints are selected by GMS uniformly over the $\rho $-box (intuition: $\rho  n^{-1/2}=o_{\mathcal{P}}(\kappa _{n}^{-1})$),\\
 & and $\Vert \hat{\xi}_n(\theta_n^\prime) - \kappa_n^{-1}\sqrt{n}\sigma_{P_n,j}^{-1}(\theta_n^\prime)E_{P_n}[m_j(X_i,\theta_n^\prime)] \Vert =o_\mathcal{P}(1)$. \\
[0.15cm]
Lemma \ref{lem:empt} & $\forall \eta>0 ~\exists \delta>0,  : \Pr(\{\mathfrak W(c)\ne\emptyset\}\cap \{\mathfrak W^{-\delta}(c)=\emptyset\})<\eta$, and similarly for $V^I_n$. \\
 & It is unlikely that these sets are nonempty but become empty upon slightly tightening stochastic constraints.\\
[0.15cm]

 & This justifies ``merging" them.\\
[0.15cm]

To keep the notation simple, below we argue as if all j=1,dots,J belong to J^*. Consider the case that c_pi^*>0. For some c_pi^*>delta>0, let W(c-delta) equiv big\ lambdain mathfrak B^d_rho: p^prime lambda =0 &cap w_j(lambda)le c-delta , \: forall j=1,dots,Jbig\, where we emphasize that the set W(c-delta) is obtained by a delta-contraction of all constraints, including those indexed by j=J_1+1,dots,J. By Assumption , for any eta>0 there exists a delta such that eta ge leftvert Prleft(W(c_pi^*)neq emptyset right)-Prleft(W(c_pi^*-delta)neq emptyset right)rightvert = Prleft(\W(c_pi^*)neq emptyset\ cap \W(c_pi^*-delta)=emptyset\right),\\ eta ge leftvert Prleft(W(c_pi^*+delta)neq emptyset right)-Prleft(W(c_pi^*)neq emptyset right)rightvert = Prleft(\W(c_pi^*+delta)neq emptyset\ cap \W(c_pi^*)=emptyset\right). The result follows. underlineStep 2. Revisiting the proof of Lemma . Case 1 of Lemma is unaltered. Case 2 of Lemma follows from the same argument as used in Case 1 of Lemma , because under Assumption as shown in step 1 of this proof all inequalities are tightened. In Case 3 of Lemma the result in holds automatically by Assumption -(ii). (As a remark, Lemmas - are no longer needed to establish Lemma .) underlineStep 3. Revisiting the proof of Lemma . Under Assumption we do not need to merge paired inequalities. Hence, part (iii) of Lemma holds automatically because varphi^*_j(xi) le varphi_j(xi) for any j and xi. We are left to establish parts (i) and (ii) of Lemma . These follow immediately, because Lemma remains valid as shown in step 1 and by Assumption , Pr(W(c)neq emptyset) is strictly increasing at c=c_pi^* if c_pi^*>0. (As a remark, Lemma is no longer needed to establish Lemma .) In summary, the desired result follows by applying Lemma in the proof of Theorem - as Lemmas , and remain valid, Lemmas , , and the Lemmas in Appendix are unaffected, and Lemmas , , are no longer needed. Part . This is established by adapting the proof of Theorem - as follows: In the main proof, we pass to an a.s. representation early on, so that W realizes jointly with other random variables (we denote almost sure representations adding a superscript ``^*" on the original variable). At the same time, we entirely drop rho. This means that algebraic expressions, e.g. in the main proof, simplify as if rho=1, but it also removes any constraints along the lines of lambda in B^d_n,rho in equation . The next major adaptation is that in and : we again drop rho but nominally introduce the constraint that lambda in barW^*(barc). However, for c leq barc, this condition cannot constrain W^*(c), and so we can as well drop it: The modified W^*(c) equals barW^*(c). Next we argue that Lemma continues to hold, now claimed for barW^*. To verify that this is the case, replace B^d with barW(barc) throughout in Lemma . Now we compare tilde V_n^b and tilde V_n^I with widetilde barW. To ensure that lambda is uniformly stochastically bounded in expressions like , we verify that the modified tilde V_n^b and tilde V_n^I inherit the property in Assumption . To see this, fix any unit vector t perp p and notice that any t=lambda /\| lambda \| for lambda in widetilde barW(c) or for lambda in tilde V_n^b(theta_n',c) or for lambda in tilde V_n^I(theta_n',c), 0<cle bar c, satisfies this condition. By Assumption and the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, max_lambda in widetilde barW(c)t'lambda=O(1) for any c le barc. Since the value of this program is necessarily attained by a basic solution whose associated gradients span t, it must be the case that such solution is itself O(1). It follows that, by similar reasoning to the preceding paragraph, the comparison between V_n^I(theta_n',c) and barW(c) in Lemma goes through.

nodes.statement: We first show . If J^*=emptyset, with J^* as defined in , then the result is immediate. Assume then that J^* neq emptyset. Any inequality indexed by j notin J^* is satisfied with probability approaching one by similar arguments as in (both with c and with c-delta). Hence, one could argue for sets mathfrak W(c),mathfrak W^-delta(c) defined as in equations and but with j in J^*. To keep the notation simple, below we argue as if all j=1,dots,J belong to J^*. Let c ge 0 be given. Let g be a J+2d+2 vector with entries g_j =left\ lll c - Z_j, & j=1,dots,J,\\ 1, & j=J+1,dots,J+2d,\\ 0, & j=J+2d+1,J+2d+2, right. recalling that pi_1,j^*=0 for j=J_1+1,cdots,J. Let tau be a (J+2d+2) vector with entries tau_j = left\ ll 1, & j =1,dots,J_1, \\ 0, & j =J_1+1,dots,J+2d+2. right. Then we can express the sets of interest as mathfrak W(c) &= \lambda: Klambda le g\,\\ mathfrak W^-delta(c)&= \lambda: Klambda le g-delta tau\. By Farkas' Lemma, e.g. citet[Theorem 22.1]Rockafellar1970a, a solution to the system of linear inequalities in exists if and only if for all mu in R^J+2d+2_+ such that mu^primeK=0, one has mu^primeg ge 0. Similarly, a solution to the system of linear inequalities in exists if and only if for all mu in R^J+2d+2 such that mu^primeK=0, one has mu^prime(g-delta tau) ge 0. Define mathcal Mequiv \ muinmathbb R^J+2d+2_+:mu' K=0\. Then, one may write &~Pr(\mathfrak W(c)ne emptyset \ cap \W^-delta(theta_n^prime,c)= emptyset \ )notag\\ =&~Pr(\mu'gge 0, forallmuin mathcal M\cap \mu'(g-delta tau)< 0, existsmuin mathcal M\)notag \\ = &~Pr(\mu'gge 0, forallmuin mathcal M\cap\ mu'g< deltamu'tau, existsmuin mathcal M\) . Note that the set mathcal M is a non-stochastic polyhedral cone which may change with n. By Minkowski-Weyl's theorem (see, e.g. citet[Theorem 3.52]Rockafellar_Wets2005aBK), for each n there exist \nu^tin mathcal M,t=1,cdots, T\, with T<infty a constant that depends only on J and d, such that any muinmathcal M can be represented as mu=b sum_t=1^T a_tnu^t, where b>0 and a_tge 0, ~t=1,dots,T, ~sum_t=1^T a_t=1. Hence, if muinmathcal M satisfies mu'g< deltamu'tau, denoting nu^t prime the transpose of vector nu^t, we have sum_t=1^T a_tnu^t primeg<deltasum_t=1^T a_tnu^t primetau. However, due to a_tge 0,forall t and nu^tinmathcal M, this means nu^tprimeg< deltanu^t primetau for some tin\1,dots,T\. Furthermore, since nu^tinmathcal M, we have 0le nu^tprimeg. Therefore, Prleft(\mu'gge 0, forallmuin mathcal M\cap\mu'g< delta mu^prime tau, existsmuin mathcal M\right)\\ le Prleft(0lenu^tprimeg< deltanu^tprimetau,exists tin\1,cdots,T\right) le sum_t=1^T Prleft(0lenu^tprimeg< deltanu^tprimetau right). Case 1. Consider first any t =1,dots,T such that nu^t assigns positive weight only to constraints in \J+1,dots,J+2d+2\. Then nu^t prime g&=sum_j=J+1^J+2dnu^t_j,\\ deltanu^t prime tau &=deltasum_j=J+1^J+2d+2nu^t_j tau_j=0, where the last equality follows by . Therefore Prleft(0lenu^tprimeg< deltanu^tprimetau right)=0. Case 2. Consider now any t = 1,dots,T such that nu^t assigns positive weight also to constraints in \1,dots,J\. Recall that indices j=J_1+1,dots,J_1+2J_2 correspond to moment equalities, each of which is written as two moment inequalities, therefore yielding a total of 2J_2 inequalities with D_j+J_2 = - D_j for j =J_1+1,dots,J_1+J_2, and: g = left\ll c - Z_j & j =J_1+1,dots,J_1+J_2, \\ c + Z_j-J_2 & j =J_1+J_2+1,dots,J. right. By Assumption , there exists a constant omega>0 such that the smallest eigenvalue of Omega is bounded from below by omega for all theta_n^prime. This establishes equation . To see why equation holds, observe that the bootstrap distribution is conditional on X_1,dots,X_n. This implies that the set hatM_n, defined as the set in equation () but with hatK_n replacing K, can be treated as nonstochastic as well. Then one can mimic the argument following to conclude . The results in - follow by similar arguments, with proper redefinition of tau in equation .

Fix any $c \geq 0$ and restrict attention to constraints $\{J_1+1,...,J_1+d,J_1+J_2+1,...,J_1+J_2+d\}$, i.e. the inequalities that jointly correspond to the first $d$ equalities. We separately analyze the case when (i) the corresponding estimated gradients $\{\hat{D}_{n,j}(\theta):j = J_1+1,...,J_1+d\}$ are linearly independent and (ii) they are not. If $\{\hat{D}_{n,j}(\theta):j = J_1+1,...,J_1+d\}$ converge to linearly independent limits, then only the former case occurs infinitely often; else, both may occur infinitely often, and we conduct the argument along two separate subsequences if necessary.

For the remainder of this proof, because the sequence $\{\theta_n\}$ is fixed and plays no direct role in the proof, we suppress dependence of $\hat{D}_{n,j}(\theta)$ and $\mathbb{G}^b_{n,j}(\theta)$ on $\theta$. Also, if $C$ is an index set picking certain constraints, then $\hat{D}_{n}^C$ is the matrix collecting the corresponding estimated gradients, and similarly for $\mathbb{G}_{n}^{b,C}$.

Suppose now case (i), then there exists an index set ${\bar C}\subset \{J_1+1,...,J_1+d,J_1+J_2+1,\dots,J_1+J_2+d\}$ picking one direction of each constraint s.t. $p$ is a positive linear combination of the rows of $\hat{D}_{P}^{\bar C}$. (This choice ensures that a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker condition holds, justifying the step from \eqref{eq:cbd_s1} to \eqref{eq:cbd_s3} below.) Then the  coverage probability $P^*(V^I_n(\theta,c)\ne\emptyset)$ is asymptotically bounded above by
\begin{align}
P^* \Big( \sup_{\lambda \in \rho B^d_{n,\rho}} \Big\{ p^{\prime }\lambda:\hat{D}_{n,j}\lambda \leq c-\mathbb{G}_{n,j}^b,j \in \mathcal{J}^{*}\Big\} \geq 0 \Big) \leq &~ P^* \Big( \sup_{\lambda \in \mathbb{R}^d} \Big\{ p^{\prime }\lambda:\hat{D}_{n,j}\lambda \leq c-\mathbb{G}_{n,j}^b,j \in \bar C\Big\} \geq 0 \Big) \label{eq:cbd_s1}\\
=&~ P^* \Big(p^{\prime} (\hat{D}_{n}^{\bar C})^{-1}(c\mathbf{1}_d-\mathbb{G}^{b,\bar C}_n) \geq 0 \Big) \label{eq:cbd_s3}\\
=&~ P^* \bigg( \frac{p^{\prime} (\hat{D}_{n}^{\bar C})^{-1}(c\mathbf{1}_d-\mathbb{G}^{b,\bar C}_n)}{\sqrt{p^\prime(\hat{D}_{n}^{\bar C})^{-1}\Omega_P^C (\hat{D}_{n}^{\bar C})^{-1}p}} \geq 0 \bigg)\label{eq:cbd_s4} \\
=&~ P^* \bigg( \frac{p^{\prime} adj(\hat{D}_{n}^{\bar C})(c\mathbf{1}_d-\mathbb{G}^{b,\bar C}_n)}{\sqrt{p^\prime(adj(\hat{D}_{n}^{\bar C})\Omega_P^C adj(\hat{D}_{n}^{\bar C})p}} \geq 0 \bigg)\label{eq:cbd_s4b} \\
=&~ \Phi \bigg(\frac{p^\prime adj(\hat{D}_{n}^{\bar C})c\mathbf{1}_d}{\sqrt{p^\prime(adj(\hat{D}_{n}^{\bar C})\Omega_P^C adj(\hat{D}_{n}^{\bar C})p}} \bigg) + o_{\mathcal{P}}(1) \label{eq:cbd_s5}\\
\leq &~ \Phi (d \omega^{-1/2} c) + o_{\mathcal{P}}(1).\label{eq:cbd_s6}
\end{align}
Here, \eqref{eq:cbd_s1} removes constraints and hence enlarges the feasible set; \eqref{eq:cbd_s3} solves in closed form; \eqref{eq:cbd_s4} divides through by a positive scalar; \eqref{eq:cbd_s4b} eliminates the determinant of $\hat{D}_{n}^{\bar C}$, using that rows of $\hat{D}_{n}^{\bar C}$ can always be rearranged so that the determinant is positive; \eqref{eq:cbd_s5} follows by Assumption \ref{as:bcs1}, using that the term multiplying $\mathbb{G}^{b,\bar C}_{n}$ is $O_{\mathcal{P}}(1)$; and \eqref{eq:cbd_s6} uses that by Assumption \ref{as:correlation}, there exists a constant $\omega>0$ that does not depend on $\theta$ such that the smallest eigenvalue of $\Omega_P$ is bounded from below by $\omega$. The result follows for any choice of $\underline{c} \in (0,\Phi
	^{-1}(1-\alpha )\times  \omega^{1/2}/d)$.
	
In case (ii), there exists an index set $\bar C \subset \{J_1+2,...,J_1+d,J_1+J_2+2,...,J_1+J_2+d\}$ collecting $d-1$ or fewer linearly independent constraints s.t. $\hat{D}_{n,J_1+1}$ is a positive linear combination of the rows of $\hat{D}_{P}^{\bar C}$. (Note that $\bar C$ cannot contain $J_1+1$ or $J_1+J_2+1$.) One can then write
\begin{align}
&~P^* \Big( \sup_{\lambda \in \rho B^d_{n,\rho}} \Big\{ p^{\prime }\lambda:\hat{D}_{n,j}\lambda \leq c-\mathbb{G}_{n,j}^b,j \in \bar C \cup \{J_1+J_2+1\} \Big\} \geq 0 \Big) \label{eq:cbd_s7}\\
\leq &~P^* \left( \exists \lambda: \hat{D}_{n,j}\lambda \leq c-\mathbb{G}_{n,j}^b,j \in \bar C \cup \{J_1+J_2+1\} \right) \label{eq:cbd_s8}\\
\leq &~P^* \Big(\sup_{\lambda \in \rho B^d_{n,\rho}} \left\{ \hat{D}_{n,J_1+1}\lambda: \hat{D}_{n,j}\lambda \leq c-\mathbb{G}_{n,j}^b,j \in \bar C \right\} \geq \inf_{\lambda \in \rho B^d_{n,\rho}} \left\{ \hat{D}_{n,J_1+1}\lambda: \hat{D}_{n,J_1+J_2+1}\lambda \leq c-\mathbb{G}_{n,J_1+J_2+1}^b\right\} \Big)\label{eq:cbd_s9} \\
= &~P^* \left( \hat{D}_{n,J_1+1} \hat{D}^{\bar C \prime}_{n} (\hat{D}^{\bar C}_{n} \hat{D}^{\bar C \prime}_{n})^{-1} (c\mathbf{1}_{\bar d}-\mathbb{G}^{b,\bar C}_n) \geq -c+\mathbb{G}_{n,J_1+J_2+1}^b \right). \label{eq:cbd_s10}
